page: Microsoft Azure L4as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Lasv4 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 server features 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high resource density of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 960 GB NVMe SSD and is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is also strong. However, multi-core performance and overall CPU metrics, such as the Passmark CPU score and Geekbench multi-core score, fall into the average category. Memory write bandwidth is average, but read-only memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks is weak, landing in the bottom 25%. Database operations, Redis SET performance, and multi-threaded decompression also show weak benchmark results. Large-model LLM inference is poor, though small-model inference and static web serving throughput remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L4as_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and fast local NVMe storage without the premium cost of larger multi-core instances. The primary tradeoff is the moderate multi-core scaling and weak memory read bandwidth, which limits its effectiveness for memory-bound parallel computing or heavy database write operations. This profile makes the server well-suited for memory-intensive but moderately threaded workloads, such as caching layers, light database hosting, text processing, and static web serving.
